title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two halves. The left half is crossed out by a long diagonal stroke, but its diagrams are rewritten cleanly on the right.

(1) Uniformization picture. X is a (hyperbolic) Riemann surface with base point x. Pi(x) = pi_1(X,x) and Pi(x,y) are the path classes. Grothendieck builds a fibre bundle B(x) over X. Its fibre at y is the set of classes of pairs (c, xi), with c in Pi(x,y) and xi in \hat T_{X,x}, under the relation (c lambda, xi) ~ (c, lambda xi) for lambda in Pi(x).
- \hat T_{X,x} is the projective completion of the tangent line, a P^1. Pi(x) acts on it through the monodromy of the uniformizing projective structure.
- So B(x) = X~ x_{pi_1} P^1 is the flat P^1-bundle attached to uniformization.
- Sigma(x) is its canonical holomorphic section, given by the developing map, i.e. the point itself.
- The fibre P^1 splits as disc, circle and opposite disc. This splits B(x) into two open disc bundles U(x) and V(x) plus a circle bundle.
- The tangent-space picture is the model: D_x is a disc in T_{X,x}, D'_x is its P^1-completion (or the complementary disc), and \bar D_x the complementary disc.
- The labels record which identifications are real-analytic (R-an) and which complex-analytic (C-an):
  - U(x) ~ X~_(x) x_{(X,Pi(x))} \bar X_(x) is complex-analytic. This is the quotient (H x \bar H)/Gamma, a complexification of X.
  - V(x) contains the section Sigma.
  - Both U(x) and V(x) are only real-analytically isomorphic to the disc bundles D_X and D'_X of the tangent bundle.
  - \hat T_X is real-analytically isomorphic to B(x), compatibly with the zero section Sigma_X.
- So the flat P^1-bundle of the projective structure is real-analytically, but not holomorphically, the projectivised tangent bundle P(T_X + O_X). Its two hemispheres carry the two natural complex structures.

(2) The rank-2 bundle. E is the holomorphic rank-2 bundle with P(E) = B, written 'T_X + O_X = Omega^{-1} (+) Omega^0'. Here + means a (non-split, Atiyah/Gunning) extension and (+) its graded pieces.
- He computes the graded pieces of End E: rows (Omega^0, Omega^{-1}), (Omega^1, Omega^0).
- He then computes End E (x) Omega^1: rows (Omega^1, Omega^0), (Omega^2, Omega^1). The trace-free part is written V (x) Omega^1, with -Omega^1 in the corner.
- Counting sections of the graded pieces: g from Omega^1, 1 from Omega^0, 3g-3 from Omega^2. This gives g+1 and 3g-3, total 4g-2. The total is an upper bound read off the grading (two diagonal Omega^1 identified up to sign), presumably towards the dimension of the space of connections or Higgs fields on E.
- A crossed-out degree matrix (1 0 / 2g-2 1) and '2g' are discarded.
- Omega^1 = omega^{(x)2} records the theta-characteristic (square root of K) underlying the Gunning bundle.

(3) Bottom. This continues the 'écart' calculus of the neighbouring pages (cocycles c(f) attached to local coordinates, invariant under groups G acting on f).
- For the group Z/2 . G_m, acting by f -> c f^{+-1} (the 'Ecmu_2' of the next page), he looks for invariants. h = f + 1/f = (f^2+1)/f is invariant under f -> 1/f. One recovers f from h via f^2 - f h + 1 = 0 (x^2 = 1, x = +-1 are the fixed points). He notes h has no zeros/poles condition ('sans zéro').
- He sets phi = g/g', the inverse of the logarithmic derivative, and integrates back: log g = int 1/phi, so g = c exp int 1/phi.
- This checks that the quotient E*_X/(G_m) is identified with omega^1* via df/f, and how the Z/2 quotient squares it.
errors: The dimension count 4g-2 is read off the graded pieces (g+1 + 3g-3). For the non-split Gunning extension the actual h^0 of End_0(E)(x)Omega^1 need not equal the sum over graded pieces; no exactness/vanishing argument is given on the page.

Notation for E is ambiguous ('T_X+O_X = Omega^{-1}(+)Omega^0'): an extension is conflated with its associated graded. Harmless as bookkeeping, but literally false holomorphically for the uniformizing structure (the extension is non-split).
'f+1/f sans zéro' is not literally correct: f+1/f vanishes where f = +-i. Presumably a condition on the domain or on h is intended.

ideas.what: Flat P^1-bundle over X associated with the uniformizing/projective structure, built as pairs (path class, point of P(T_x+C)) modulo pi_1, with canonical section given by the developing map
ideas.modern_name: Projective structure as flat PGL2-bundle with transverse section (Gunning/Ehresmann; precursor of PGL2-opers)

ideas.what: Splitting the flat P^1-bundle into two hemisphere disc bundles; the one avoiding the section is C-analytically the quotient (X~ x conj X~)/pi_1, while both are only R-analytically the tangent disc bundles
ideas.modern_name: Bers simultaneous uniformization / complexification (H x \bar H)/Gamma; Grauert tube (adapted complex structure) of a hyperbolic surface
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bers (1960); Guillemin-Stenzel, Lempert-Szőke (1991), Burns for adapted complex structures

ideas.what: Rank-2 bundle E with graded pieces Omega^{-1}, Omega^0 (theta characteristic Omega^1 = omega^2), with graded computation of End E and End E (x) Omega^1 and count 4g-2
ideas.modern_name: Gunning/Atiyah bundle (jet bundle J^1(K^{-1/2}) twisted), oper Higgs-field/connection counting

ideas.what: Invariants of the group f -> c f^{+-1} (f+1/f) and recovery of a function from phi = g/g' by g = c exp int 1/phi, within the 'écart' cocycle calculus
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/cocycle description of multiplicative structures; elementary invariant theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck places, in one diagram, the flat P^1-bundle of uniformization, its two hemisphere disc bundles, and the complexification X~ x_{pi_1} conj X~. He records that they are complex-analytically canonical yet only real-analytically the tangent disc bundles. This is essentially the later Grauert-tube / adapted-complex-structure picture for hyperbolic surfaces, here phrased via projective structures in his 'écart' framework. The picture itself is known (Bers, Szőke, Burns); only its appearance in Grothendieck's notes is unrecorded.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck thinking about projective structures and the PGL2-bundle-with-section viewpoint (proto-opers) around the Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs material.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is classical: the uniformization flat P^1-bundle, Bers-type complexification and the Gunning rank-2 bundle with a graded dimension count. It is interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's unpublished work on projective structures and Schwarzian 'écarts', but contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'B(x)_y = dim [?] de [?] de [?] (c,ξ)' likely reads 'B(x)_y = ensemble des classes de couples (c,ξ)' (equivalence classes of pairs).
'w/ droits [?]' under Π_1(X,x) probably 'à droite' (right action of π_1).
'Π_x × Π_x' is likely 'Π_x × Π_x' acting (or Π_x × \bar Π_x).
'GP(1,C)' should be read as the projective group of P^1 (PGL(2,C)/P(1,C)), as on the next page 'P(1,C)'.
The bottom crossed-out matrix region contains '2g' crossed out near 'g = -∫ d f^{-1}' (likely g = -∫ df/f or similar); the inline '2g' crossed item is a degree/genus count, not a function.
'$\hat T_X^* + O_X$' with an asterisk above: probably the extension T_X + O_X (projective completion of tangent bundle), consistent with the next line 'V_X + O_X = Ω^{-1} ⊕ Ω^0'.
